He was giving. Their goal was to persuade, and they put forth all effort to persuade those who should keep the law, especially in these matters. The rest of the commandments were not a major concern for them. The Savior said to them, 'Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe the anise and the cumin, and you neglect the weightier matters of the law, judgment, and mercy, and faith.' They were lovers of money and greedy, and they would bring lawsuits against those who failed, in order to gain more. He says to those who are being wronged by them, 'My people, your rulers oppress you, and those who collect taxes dominate you.' He says this to the people, and still gives Israel to understand, that if they were to follow him, they would attain humanity and philanthropy, and would not fall away from their relationship with him. By saying that the rulers 'oppress', he shows the magnitude of their greed and love of money. For in the threshing floors, some beat out the grain with iron, while others gather the fallen grain, leaving nothing behind. This is also a custom among those who harvest grapes. He says, 'Your rulers oppress you.' It is as if he were saying, 'They have squeezed your possessions, and their greed is not satisfied with that.'

pass_b_english: …The Savior criticized the scribes and Pharisees, saying they were hypocrites who focused on minor details of the law, such as tithing the anise and the cumin, while neglecting the more important aspects, like judgment, mercy, and faith (Matthew 23:23).

They were driven by greed and a love of money, which led them to oppress and dominate others, and they would bring lawsuits against those who failed, in order to gain more, and even beyond what they were capable of, they would still try to extract more (Matthew 23:23).

He warned the people that their rulers were taking advantage of them, and that they should not follow their example, saying, 'My people, your rulers oppress you, and those who collect taxes dominate you' (Matthew 23:12, Isaiah 3:12).

The Savior's words were a call to the people to recognize the hypocrisy of their leaders and to seek a more authentic and compassionate way of living, striving to be humane and philanthropic, and to maintain a good relationship with God.
He used the metaphor of threshing floors and grape harvests to illustrate the extent of the rulers' greed and oppression, emphasizing the severity of their actions and the need for change.

But already they are laying hands on and pressuring those who are still left, dominating them with an iron fist, rather than guiding them gently as teachers should, forcing their own thoughts and desires upon their followers, rather than allowing them to grow and learn in a nurturing environment.

But this was not the goal of those who followed Christ, who were called to be examples of the flock, not lording their power over others, as the apostle Peter encouraged those who were called to oversee and guide the flock to do so in a humble and servant-like manner (1 Peter 5:3).

The mystical word, or the deeper spiritual truth, recognizes that there are other forces at work, other practitioners who seek to dominate and control, and it is necessary for those who want to live a life of integrity and righteousness to avoid these influences, for there are evil powers that oppose us, that seek to turn our minds and hearts towards what is vile and corrupt, and they demand from us a kind of tax, a payment in the form of our inclination towards passion and sin.
And indeed the holy one blesses…
